cpap-vs-peep-terminology.userTake: CPAP is the non-invasive name (mask) and PEEP is the invasive name (through a ventilator/ET tube) for the same continuous-pressure idea.

continuous-pressure-in-cpap-peep.userTake: You dial in a pressure, not a volume — it stays the same whether the patient is breathing in or breathing out.

cpap-and-peep-setting-range.userTake: Both CPAP and PEEP get dialed in somewhere in the 5 to 20 cm H2O range.

cpap-for-obstructive-sleep-apnea.userTake: The constant pressure holds the tongue forward so the airway doesn't obstruct — that's why CPAP helps with sleep apnea specifically in the non-invasive setting.

peep-alveolar-recruitment.userTake: PEEP holds the little alveolar clusters open at the end of exhale instead of letting them collapse — turning up PEEP recruits more of them.

pressure-support-ventilation.userTake: Pressure support only fires on a patient-triggered breath and delivers a set pressure instead of a set volume — no backup rate, and it's a common weaning mode.

peep-recruits-alveoli-for-oxygenation.userTake: Higher PEEP recruits more alveoli, and more recruited alveoli means better oxygenation.
peep-recruits-alveoli-for-oxygenation.userBody: At the end of exhalation, PEEP leaves a set amount of pressure in the circuit to recruit alveoli. The higher the PEEP dial, the more alveoli get recruited -- and more recruited alveoli means better oxygenation. (edited to lead with the clinical takeaway)
